findings.evidence: `isZero_res_coindBot` at line 385 already works for arbitrary ambient `G`; the extra hypothesis enters the induced proof only through `indBotIsoCoindBot` at line 395, an avoidable global finite-group comparison. Line 399 inherits the same avoidable restriction.
findings.fix: Prove the restriction analogue for `indBot` using a coset decomposition, remove `[Finite G]` from both theorems, and derive the regular case from the unconditional `indBot ≅ leftRegular` part of the existing construction.
findings.issue: `isZero_res_indBot` and `isZero_res_leftRegular` (line 399) impose `[Finite G]`, although restriction of a module induced from the trivial subgroup decomposes into induced modules over `S` independently of the size of `G`.

summary: The restricted induced and regular acyclicity theorems unnecessarily require the ambient group to be finite; only the subgroup computing Tate cohomology must be finite.
